verdicts.corrected_location: native/Packages/JunoNativeKit/Sources/JunoDesignKit/DesignDocument.swift:479-537 (struct and CodingKeys); round trip at DesignBridge.swift:128 and DesktopArtifactCanvas.swift:1068,1076-1079
verdicts.reasoning: READ: TS BaseNode requires cornerSmoothing (src/lib/design/types.ts:484), and the schema defaults it to 0 (schema.ts:332). The Swift DesignNode properties and CodingKeys (DesignDocument.swift:479-537) have no such field. `rg cornerSmoothing -g '*.swift' native` returns nothing; the only native hit is the bundled editor.js. The decoder is a plain JSONDecoder (DesignDocumentCodec.swift:54), and nothing keeps unknown keys, so the field is dropped. The bridge re-decodes every transaction through DesignDocumentCodec.load, which calls decode (DesignBridge.swift:128, Codec:135). DesktopDesignSurface decodes the stored body on open (DesktopArtifactCanvas.swift:1068) and re-encodes each transaction into the draft (1076-1079). openDocument is built from the Swift struct through jsonObject/encode (DesignBridge.swift:194-199, 217-219), so the editor never receives the smoothing either. History check: types.ts gained only cornerSmoothing in c69ee98e (15 Aug), after the last Swift model and test commits (6-7 Aug), and no Swift test fixture mentions it. The iPhone library editor (JunoMobileWorkspaceViews.swift:2061-2066) has the same onEdit draft path. Silent loss of styling data on every Mac or iPhone save stays high.

READ: saveArtifact reads artifact.currentVersion from `artifacts` at save time (NativeArtifactStore.swift:321-335). The Mac root fans every sync generation into artifactModel.synchronizationDidAdvance, which calls reload() and replaces `artifacts` (JunoDesktopRootView.swift:69-80; NativeArtifactStore.swift:252-265). DesktopDesignSurface reads `content` once by design (DesktopArtifactCanvas.swift:975-979). Its identity is keyed only on design.id and designReloadToken (DesktopDesignScreen.swift:435), and nothing calls host.adopt. After v4 lands, isDirty compares the v3-based draft with v4 (239-242), and Save posts baseVersion 4. The server compares only baseVersion with currentVersion (src/app/api/artifacts/[id]/route.ts:50-55), so it accepts the save and overwrites v4. On a 409, performMutation merges the latest version (NativeArtifactStore.swift:422-426), and the screen's own comment names a second Save as the recovery (DesktopDesignScreen.swift:574-582). That second Save overwrites v4 the same way. The Liquid Glass branch does not change this.

READ: the draft lives only in @State (DesktopDesignScreen.swift:215). 'All designs' calls closeDesign() (444-446), which sets draft = nil (520-523) with no prompt, and .onAppear also calls closeDesign() (264). The screen is one arm of the destination switch (DesktopAccountScreens.swift:120-134), so switching destination tears down its state. rg finds no onDisappear, applicationShouldTerminate or unsaved-changes guard for design anywhere in native/macOS/JunoDesktop/App. The .onChange(of: openDesign == nil) path (261-263) also discards when the account model empties. Silent loss of user work.

verdicts.corrected_location: .github/workflows/release-macos.yml:141-143 and native/Scripts/release-macos.sh (no editor check); tests/design-host-bridge.test.ts:77 (misleading title)
verdicts.reasoning: READ and RUN: `node scripts/build-design-editor.mjs --check` exits 1 with 'bundle is stale (expected 1.0.0+9cc1cfa8d4fe)', while index.html stamps 1.0.0+2b86e5baaf9d. The last bundle commit is 2fa09d35 (17 Sept). Eleven editor commits follow before the release commit 0a3087fe, 16 files and +1161/-491 lines, including host/editor.css (+64) and main.tsx. The shipped editor.css/js contain no `after:scale-x-100` and no `data-motion`. The test at tests/design-host-bridge.test.ts:77 never compares the hash. CORRECTION: the auditor's claim that nothing in CI runs the check is wrong. .github/workflows/release-ios.yml:76 runs `npm run design:editor:check`, so the current tree would fail the next iOS production release until someone rebuilds. What is true is that the macOS release workflow (release-macos.yml:141-143 runs test/lint/build only), native.yml, release-gates.sh and release-macos.sh (the ad-hoc --publish-dev path Mac 1.6.0 shipped through) never check freshness. The effects are visual and UX divergence, not data loss, so medium rather than high.

READ: Tailwind --content is limited to src/components/design/** plus icon-swap.tsx (build-design-editor.mjs:172). The editor imports ui/button, tooltip, dropdown-menu, popover, select, kbd, collapse, menu-recipe and icons (rg of imports). The shipped editor.js really uses the unscanned classes: its menu shell string is 'surface-float overlay-glass z-popper … data-[state=open]:animate-pop-in', and the ui-button base contains 'inline-flex … whitespace-nowrap' and 'icon-sm':'size-8'. The shipped editor.css has 0 hits for .inline-flex, .size-8{, .h-8{, whitespace-nowrap, surface-float, overlay-glass, z-popper, animate-pop-in, animate-tooltip-in, control-primary and --shadow-float. surface-float, control-neu and control-primary are defined only in globals.css (1137, 1154 and nearby), and host/editor.css defines none of them. z-popper, shadow-float and bg-selected would read --z-popper, --shadow-float and --selected, which the host never declares, so scanning ui/ alone would not fix them either. The editor's menu call sites pass only width classes (e.g. design-editor.tsx:671, MENU_W), and TOOL_KEY (design-editor.tsx:115) sets no size, so toolbar buttons depend entirely on Button's own classes. The rendered result is INFERRED from the missing rules, but the evidence is strong. Note: `inline-flex` and `size-8` also appear in current design sources, so a rebuild would restore those two by accident. The surface classes need host CSS or a wider scan.

READ: host editor.css sets --primary 231 82% 63%, --background 0 0% 100% and --border 240 6% 90%, with a hue-240 dark palette (15-35, 67-85). globals.css has --primary 15 54% 46% (80), --background 48 24% 97.2% (68) and dark 30 5% 11.5% (505), and FLAT_UI §3.1 says every rung stays warm. The header (editor.css:4-6) claims identical values, which is false. The shipped CSS has `.text-destructive{color:hsl(var(--destructive-ink)/…)}` and `.text-primary{color:hsl(var(--primary-ink)/…)}`, because tailwind.config.ts:472-480 routes text-* through the *-ink ramps. Neither ink variable is declared in the host, so both declarations are invalid at computed-value time and fall back to the inherited colour. That makes destructive text and primary text foreground-coloured. .shadow-soft reads the undeclared --shadow-soft. Nothing passes JunoAccentSelection into the web view (no accent reference in DesktopDesignEditorHost.swift or main.tsx).

READ: exportAs fetches the relative URL `/api/design/${artifactId}/export` (design-editor.tsx:304). The hosted document is file:// (DesktopDesignEditorHost.swift:121), and the CSP has connect-src 'none' (build-design-editor.mjs:105), so the fetch rejects and the catch shows a toast (340-341). main.tsx:66 passes session.document.id, the DesignDocument id rather than the artifact id. Even a successful fetch would then hit saveBlob's blob/anchor download, which the navigation policy cancels (209-214 allows file URLs only), and there is no download delegate. The Export dropdown renders unconditionally (656-682). The Design screen's ⋯ menu offers only Delete (DesktopDesignScreen.swift:486-497). Export exists only in the separate Artifacts library.

READ: image placement and replacement use hidden `<input type=file>` elements (design-canvas.tsx:1268-1276; inspector-panel.tsx:1275). The host's WKUIDelegate conformance implements only createWebViewWith (DesktopDesignEditorHost.swift:199-234), and rg finds no runOpenPanel anywhere in native. On macOS, WKWebView treats a missing runOpenPanelWith as Cancel, so no panel appears. The asset path itself is local (readImageAsset uses a data URL, use-design-document.ts:582-607), so the picker is the only blocker. design-canvas has no onDrop or dataTransfer handling, and a file dropped on the web view would be a file:// navigation outside the editor directory, which the policy cancels. The iPhone is unaffected, because iOS WKWebView presents the picker itself.

READ: save() captures draft (DesktopDesignScreen.swift:578), awaits saveArtifact, which includes the network request, syncModel.refresh and reload (NativeArtifactStore.swift:417-421), and then sets self.draft = nil unconditionally (581). Meanwhile onEdit keeps writing newer drafts (428), and the surface is not disabled during the save. The race is real. Downgraded because the next transaction writes the whole current document back into draft, which restores the dirty state with every in-flight edit. Loss needs the user to leave, without another edit, right after a save that raced edits, which compounds mac-design-3.

READ: launcherContent branches only on designs.isEmpty (DesktopDesignScreen.swift:372-379), and rg for phase or loading in the file finds nothing on the launcher. NativeArtifactModel exposes .loading, .offline and .failed (NativeArtifactStore.swift:193-199, 271-287). A failed load leaves `artifacts` empty on first start, and one corrupt version record fails the whole load (NativeArtifactStore.swift:93-99, 148-152). Downgraded: the list is projected from the local encrypted DB, so the loading window is short. The misleading copy matters mainly on a fresh install before the first sync, or on a failed or decryption-error load.

READ: main.tsx:65-71 passes no `surface`, so the editor defaults to 'embedded' (design-editor.tsx:176). The rails use 'hidden md:flex' and 'hidden lg:flex' (549-550). The CollapsedRail stubs and PaneResizers reuse the same visibility classes (711-714, 765, 826, 867-870), so no re-open control survives. The shipped CSS uses Tailwind's default 768/1024px breakpoints; tailwind.config.ts:44 overrides only container 2xl. The web full-page editor passes surface="window" (design-workspace.tsx:213). The default window is 1240pt wide (JunoDesktopApp.swift:148), so the inspector disappears whenever the web view drops below 1024pt, for example with the sidebar open in a narrower window.

READ: window error and unhandledrejection events post a failure (main.tsx:126-127; bridge.ts:136-137). The host sets status = .failed on any failure (DesktopDesignEditorHost.swift:172-173) and never resets it, because `ready` is sent once. The surface overlays an opaque JunoEmptyState on .failed (DesktopArtifactCanvas.swift:1052-1054), with no retry. The trigger is still INFERRED, but it is plausible: design-canvas.tsx:220-221 uses a ResizeObserver, and WebKit reports 'ResizeObserver loop completed with undelivered notifications' as a window error. CORRECTION to the failure scenario: the overlay sits inside DesktopDesignSurface, so the native Save button in the command bar stays usable, and the draft can be saved before leaving. Also, after .failed, send() is gated on .ready (140-141), so adopt() can no longer resync the editor.

READ: the navigation and UI delegate implement only decidePolicyFor, didFail, didFailProvisionalNavigation and createWebViewWith (DesktopDesignEditorHost.swift:199-234). There is no webViewWebContentProcessDidTerminate, so status stays .ready over a blank web view. The draft survives in DesktopDesignScreen state, so Save still works. The failure is confusing but recoverable by reopening. Low.

READ: the native documentCommandBar (Back, title/subtitle, Discard, Save, ⋯) plus a Divider (DesktopDesignScreen.swift:421-438, 442-501) sits above the editor's own toolbar row: tools, undo/redo, align, Motion, Export and a Saving indicator (design-editor.tsx:552-706). That toolbar is `bg-card/40` over a solid host background, so it reads as opaque. The result is two chrome rows before the canvas, with the native Save separated from the web undo. The Liquid Glass branch changes only doc comments and the sidebar icon in these files, not this layout.

READ: the web httpTransport POSTs every transaction to /api/design/[id]/transactions (use-design-document.ts:89-107). The bridge transport posts to the host and returns ok immediately (bridge.ts:114-128). The host treats the editor's `save` message as a no-op (DesktopDesignEditorHost.swift:167-170), and persistence waits for the manual native Save (DesktopDesignScreen.swift:478-484). The status is a caption subtitle ('Unsaved changes', 503-509). The same editor has two save models.

READ: the host dark palette is hue 240 zinc (editor.css:67-85), against warm hue-30 values in globals.css:505ff and FLAT_UI.md:48-62. The accent is user-selectable natively (JunoColors.swift:139-144, applied at JunoDesktopRootView.swift:86-89), and nothing sends it into the web view. This overlaps mac-design-6.

READ: Design is one arm of the destination switch in the detail column (DesktopAccountScreens.swift:120-134). The only scenes are the main WindowGroup, Incognito, Settings, Code Settings and Shortcuts (JunoDesktopApp.swift:135-218). The only extra design window is the read-only torn-off library window (DesktopArtifactsScreen.swift:1961-1967). There is no per-design window, focus mode or full-canvas mode, and the rails collapse below 1024pt (mac-design-11).

READ: the shortcut handler returns unless document.activeElement is inside the editor root (design-editor.tsx:421), handles ⌘Z/⌘D/⌘G/⌘A/⌘[ ] and passes every other chord through (468). There are no ⌘C/⌘V/⌘X bindings anywhere in src/components/design. Copy and Paste exist only as context-menu items backed by a module-level clipboard (design-context-menu.tsx:59-66, 209-221). DesktopCommands has no undo or clipboard wiring, so the Edit menu never reflects design state. NUANCE: 'after clicking Save, ⌘Z goes to the Edit menu' is uncertain. A mouse click on a SwiftUI or AppKit button does not normally take first responder, so the web view may keep key focus. Clicking into the sidebar or another native field does move focus away.

missed.title: The Mac Design screen has no Ask Juno or AI path: the editor's selection crosses the bridge and is stored, but nothing consumes it
missed.evidence: READ: HostedEditor mounts DesignEditor with no onAskJuno (main.tsx:65-71), so the toolbar's Ask Juno button (design-editor.tsx:684-690) never renders on Mac or iPhone. The host records `selection` (DesktopDesignEditorHost.swift:164-165), and DesignBridge.swift:40 documents it as driving 'the native inspector chrome and "Ask Juno"'. rg finds no reader of host.selection in DesktopArtifactCanvas.swift, DesktopDesignScreen.swift or DesktopArtifactsScreen.swift, and the Design screen's command bar has no AI entry (DesktopDesignScreen.swift:442-501).
missed.failure_scenario: A Mac user selects a card in the Design screen and wants Juno to restyle it. There is no Ask Juno control and no way to send the selection to a conversation, although the website offers one. This blocks the planned merge, in which design is edited with the model inside the conversation, on the Mac surface.

missed.title: The next iOS production release is blocked: its gate runs the editor freshness check, which the committed tree fails
missed.evidence: RUN: `node scripts/build-design-editor.mjs --check` exits 1 on HEAD d0997af2 (stale; expected 1.0.0+9cc1cfa8d4fe, shipped 1.0.0+2b86e5baaf9d). release-ios.yml:76 runs `npm run design:editor:check` under `set -euo pipefail`, before the tests and the build. The macOS release workflow does not run this check, so the two platforms' gates disagree.
missed.failure_scenario: The owner dispatches the iOS production release from main. The gate step fails at design:editor:check before any build, and no one has been warned by the Mac release or push CI, which never run the check. Meanwhile the Mac keeps shipping the stale bundle.
